chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and from him, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, who said:

I presented the book to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and he said: 'It is correct. Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the wergild (blood money) for injuries to all limbs, in the head and the face and the rest of the body, concerning hearing and vision and voice and intellect and the two hands and the two feet, regarding cutting and breaking and dysfunction and tearing and bone-exposing injury and bloody injury and displacement of bones and piercing, which occur in any of those.'

So whatever bone was broken, set properly without deformity or defect, and its bones were not displaced, its wergild is known. If it was exposed (bone visible) and its bones were not displaced, then its wergild is for the break and for the exposure. For the wergild of every broken bone is known; and the displacement of its bones is half the wergild of its break, and the wergild of its exposure is a quarter of the wergild of its break.
So whatever is covered by the clothes, apart from the two forearms and the fingers, and in a wound that does not heal, is a third of the wergild of that bone in which it is.

And he issued a verdict regarding the piercing when it is pierced from a spear or a dagger in any part of the man's extremities, so its wergild is a tenth of the wergild of the man, being one hundred dinars.

key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or compensation for injury/death

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on blood money for broken and exposed bones?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam al-Rida (AS) via his father Imam al-Hadi (AS), validates the comprehensive legal framework for *diyah* (blood money) established by Imam Ali (AS) in *al-Kafi*. It provides a detailed jurisprudential taxonomy for injuries, distinguishing between fractures, exposed bones, and nerve damage, thereby illustrating the precision of early Shia legal methodology in quantifying compensation for bodily harm.
